summary: Gaeng ho (แกงโฮะ) is a Northern Thai dry, savory stir-fry of glass noodles with curry and mixed vegetables; versions commonly include pork and pickled bamboo shoots. KHOEI Chiang Mai currently lists it, making this an easy-to-order example in Santitham.
whyGo: Try a less familiar Lanna dish with a distinctive mix of curry, herbs and soft glass noodles.
KHOEI’s current online menu confirms the dish is available for ฿105 before VAT.
bestFor: Curious eaters who enjoy savory, herbal, mildly to moderately spicy stir-fries.
Sharing several Northern Thai dishes at a sit-down meal.
skipIf: You need a reliably vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free or allergen-controlled meal; the recipe and kitchen handling are not confirmed, so ask first.
You dislike curry seasoning, pungent herbs or mixed textures.
duration: Allow about 45–75 minutes for a meal; this is a planning estimate, not a service-time guarantee.
cost: KHOEI lists gaeng ho at ฿105; menu prices exclude VAT and may change. Allow roughly ฿120–฿200 per person for this dish and a simple rice/drink order; the latter is a planning estimate.
hours: KHOEI Chiang Mai publishes daily hours of 08:00–00:00, last order 23:30. It advises calling ahead on public holidays.
bestTime: Lunch or early dinner for an easy meal. December is a busy travel period; reserve for dinner or a group, and confirm holiday hours.
gettingThere: KHOEI is at 14 Santitham Road, Chang Phueak. From Santitham Five-Way Intersection, enter YMCA Lane; the restaurant is beside Sunshine House. A songthaew or ride-hail from the Old City is a practical option; agree the songthaew fare before riding. Parking is available across the street for about 10 cars. Travel time and fare vary; check a live map and ask the driver.
booking: No booking is needed to order the dish, but KHOEI recommends reserving for dinner, holidays and larger groups. Call +66 93 138 5553 or message its LINE account; confirm the dish is still available and the current price.
accessibility: The restaurant publishes cross-street parking information but no detailed step-free access, toilet or seating accessibility information. Contact the venue to check specific mobility needs before travelling.
practicalTips: Gaeng ho is generally a fairly dry stir-fry rather than a soupy curry; a hotel explainer describes glass noodles, pork, bamboo shoots, kaffir lime leaves and lemongrass, with recipes varying.
Ask for a milder preparation if needed, and check whether this batch contains pork, shrimp paste, fish sauce, soy or other allergens. Do not assume a vegetarian or gluten-free version is available.
KHOEI’s listed price excludes VAT; ask staff to confirm the total before ordering.
decemberNotes: December 2026 holiday-specific hours and menus are not yet confirmed. KHOEI advises calling before public holidays; reserve ahead for dinner and check the gaeng ho is available on the day.
uncertainties: Restaurant menus, prices and opening hours can change before December 2026; verify directly shortly before visiting.
The precise recipe, heat level, allergens and vegetarian substitutions vary and are not specified for KHOEI’s gaeng ho.
